   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: John A. Boylan, Co. Down


Dear OUTLET Editors,

I would like to thank you for
the opportunity to obtain your
great Disk-Mag at such a
fantastic price as I had the
misfortune to suffer the
misplacement of most of my disks
and mail last year and unfortun-
ately had my OUTLET disks wiped
and paper communication lost.

Having no record of your
address, and being a Retained
Firefighter with very little
time, I never got around to
recontacting you until your
offer came in the post.

I use my SAM 512 TWIN DRIVE to
keep the minutes of our local
Divisional Fire Brigade Aid Fund
and to keep up with any of our
members, serving or retired, to
ensure that we can offer assist-
ance when required by them.

I use Tasword 2 for most of my
work in this but as I am finding
a little difficulty in keeping
accounts and records only using
TW2, could you recommend a cheap
or free Spreadsheet/Database
that would assist me?

We have about 500 personnel to
assist and as our work is
voluntary any expense comes out
of my own pocket which isn't
exactly overfull.

As I have been unable to keep in
contact with developments on SAM
hardware in the last 18 months I
still don't know if the mouse is
on the market yet. Here's hoping
for an update on Samstuff.

Can we have details or instruct-
ions to assist the poor Samfans
like myself who try to under-
stand the technobabble of the
BRAINS with 51 year old brains
who didn't have computers when
we were young enough to learn
easily. So, please let's have a
little pity on those who still
struggle to talk and think in
Olde English.
       Yours faithfully,

         John A. Boylan

Brian Cavers to John A. Boylan

Yes, you might consider SC_FILER
from Steve's Software, 7 Narrow
Close, Histon,Cambridge,CB4 4XX
at `12.50 or... GM-BASE from GM
SOFTWARE, 48 Main Road, Crynant,
Neath, SA10 8NP at `7.95. Both
were reviewed in OUTLET 47.

Another possibility that may be
more suitable is PBS from Hilton
Computer Services Ltd.,3 Suffolk
Drive, Guildford, Surrey,GU4 7FD
at `19.95. This is described as
suitable for small businesses.It
appears to be able to take care
of accounts etc. so this could
be ideal for what you want.

Oh and yes,the mouse is out now!
                       - Brian

From: A. Jeenes, MALVERN

Dear Editor,

I am trying to write a morse
receive program in machine code
for my SAM Coupe. To do this I
need to record on tape some
computer-generated morse for
testing purposes using the
EAR/MIC socket.


The SAM outputs the BEEP tone
through the TV speaker with only
a slight leakage to the MIC
socket. As I am unable to poke
ROM to change the OUT 254 value,
I accessed ROM1 and moved the
BEEP routine down from 61211 to
16400 and changed the OUT value.

I managed to get a tone on to
tape but instead of being a pure
note it was very chirpy even
though I had disabled inter-
rupts. I then tried switching
out both ROM0 and ROM1, which
didn't help. Can you suggest a
remedy?

I am unable to understand the
correct loading of the HL and DE
registers as mentioned in the
Tech. Manual viz:
"Make a BEEP DE-1 cycles long at
period HL*8 T States"
Does 'long' or 'period' mean
duration?

If I wanted to create a note of
800 cycles per sec. for .25 secs
should I...

Load DE with 7999 * .25

          (freq * time)

               and

Load HL with  6000000/(8*800)

(computer osc.freq. = 6000000 )
(divided by 8 x note frequency)

I must say that I was quite
impressed with the OUTLET disc
received this morning.

          Sincerely,

          Tony Jeenes

Brian Cavers to A. Jeenes

Your calculations look correct
to me and I tried it with the
BEEP CALL at &016F but I could
not think of a way (without a
tuning fork!) of verifying the
notes I generated.

DE-1 cycles long IS the duration
that the note will sound but in
CYCLES so it will vary with the
note. For a fixed note, varying
DE directly affects its duration
(the length of time the note
sounds) but if you then leave DE
alone and increase the frequency
of the note by decreasing the
value in HL then the note will
not sound for so long because
its duration is measured in
cycles - which will be shorter.

By "period",the manual means the
duration of each cycle measured
in T states.

Try experimenting with the CALL
at &016F until you grasp it.

However, this does not solve the
problem of why your recorded
tone fluctuates. I have not seen
the SAM BEEP routines but is it
fully relocatable to 16400 with
no changes - i.e., no internal
jumps or pageing out the lower
RAM where your code now is??!!

There may be some hardware fault
but why not study the TAPE SAVE
routine for clues? Has anyone
else any suggestions?
                        - Brian

From: Philip Seddon, BOLTON

Dear Ron & Brian,

I've just received Issue 58 of
OUTLET. Another great issue but
there is a bug in the OUTDEXMERG
program.

First press "S" then subject no.
If the search does not fill the
page, I get the error report:
Not understood.540:1

If it does fill  more  than  one
page, all you get on the  second
page is the message End of File.
So if you press "0" to see whole
file all you get is the message
End of File. As you said this is
a great idea - if it works O.K.!

I wonder if you or any other
OUTLET reader can help with a
problem. I am trying to write a
small program to write a league
table. Having entered the data I
then need to sort the strings in
order, I have t$ 1 to 8. They
all start with a value of 0 but
how do I keep them in numerical
order, e.g., highest first, if
t$(3)=6,t$(1)=1 and t$(5)=8,
how do I sort the string so that
it will print t$(5),t$(3),t$(1).


I read with interest the letters
and comments concerning SamCo. I
took out a subscription to the
Newsletter starting with Issue 3
which was two discs one contain-
ing the Juggler demo.

I received the May Issue 4 at
the end of April. This had in it
about the launch of the reduced
priced tape version of SAM.

On the 5th of June I had still
not received Issue 5. I phoned
SamCo and was told that this
month's issue was late and would
probably be sent out by the
following Friday.

Also in May, I ordered the Video
Digitiser which was due for
release on the 20th of May and
if you ordered before the 14th
you could have it 5 pounds
cheaper. As I write, 8th June, I
have still not received it.

         Philip Seddon

Brian Cavers to Philip Seddon

The easiest method of sorting
strings is known as the BUBBLE
SORT. It is not the fastest way
but it is the simplest to follow
how it works. Try this...

10 LET SWAP=0

20 FOR N=1 TO 7 (Your 8 minus 1)

30 IF VAL T$(N)<VAL T$(N+1) THEN
   LET Q$=T$(N):
   LET T$(N)=T$(N+1):     (swap)
   LET T$(N+1)=Q$:
   LET SWAP=1

40 NEXT N

50 IF SWAP=1 THEN GOTO 10

To reverse the order, change the
"<" in line 30 to a ">". If you
are only using values up to 9
then you can omit the two "VAL"
statements in line 30 and it
will go faster. It will also go
faster if you use a numeric
array to store the values. Very
large arrays will be VERY slow
to sort in BASIC!

Sorry about OUTDEXMERG. I hope
Alan Cox can solve this for next
month.I regret I can't guarantee
ADD-ENDER programs will work(see
WHAT ELSE in each issue!).

I've heard we've just received
all our missing Newsdisks but
they are so out of date now they
are more like "Historydisks"!
                        - Brian

From: Ron Smith, WATFORD

I received OUTLET Issue 58 O.K.

From: Brian Gaff, CHESSINGTON

A few comments, as ever from me
on last month's letters!

Sector errors:
Now I have no proof of this, but
here are my thoughts on why
Unidos can cope. The majority of
sector errors seem to be
corruption in the sector
preamble. This is the bit that
contains the sector number, and
a checksum. Now, if GDOS rejects
this sector outright if the
checksum is wrong, and Unidos
does not, you would retrieve
most of the data from it. Unidos
would of course correct the
checksum when it formatted the
track, and copied the data back.

Capacitor measurement by
computer eh? This sounds like a
classic case of re-inventing the
wheel!

As the circuit seems to be based
on an oscillator, I would guess
the measurement would be based
on the mark-space ratio
generated with differing values
of capacitor. Personally, I
would use the tried and tested
bridge system, as small hand
held units are around at cheap
prices.

The famous +3 printer bug is on
every machine with a V4.0 ROM.
The reason everyone does not
suffer is that most printers are
tolerant of it!

Speaking from memory, I recall
Cliff of Amstrad telling me that
when the +3 pages to get at its
printer driver, it 'wobbles' the
voltage on the Strobe line on
the printer port. Some printers
take exception to this, and will
not print afterwards. Quite how
the Pokes work I am not sure.

SAMCO problem:
I had a long chat with Alan
Miles recently,and he's aware of
the poor service. There are
several reasons for this. First-
ly, SAMCO was under financed,
and simply didn't have the staff
to cope. Also, there have been
problems due to the unavailabil-
ity of disc drives from Citizen,
which has made repairs very
slow. OK, that's the bad news.

The good news is that it's
almost certain that a company
has been found to invest in the
project. This will mean that
extra staff can be hired, and
this in turn should ease the
work load on the existing three
staff members - yes, just three!

There will be a few weeks when
Samco will be out of reach, but
on return, things should
improve. This is the message,
and I guess only time will tell
if it will work. I guess we just
'hang on in there'!

           Brian Gaff

From: Alan D. Cox, ST. CLEARS

Dear Brian,

I was surprised you did not
recognize my reference to IRIS
in the context of networking. In
his book on Interface 1, Ian
Logan uses SELF to denote the
sending Spectrum, and IRIS to
denote the receiver.I don't know
if he made this up: I suspect it
may be standard jargon in the
networking community - otherwise
it seems a bit pointless, except
it does allow Ian to comment
that "the use of a girl's name
makes networking just a little
more friendly". I suppose this
counts as a sexist comment these
days, heaven help us!

I note Malcolm Perry's comments
about data rates in relation to
SAM/Spectrum network compatib-
ility. In the same way that SAM
allows variable data rates for
saving to tape, it is presumably
possible in principle to vary
network data rates. If only
SAMCo would tell us a bit more
about how it all works! Perhaps
we might get a disassembly of
DOS in due course.

Re: Your letter to Nanook of the
North. I would not invest too
much money in this scheme if I
were you, or at least not for
the reason you give. The
centripetal (not centrifugal)
force needed to keep you on the
surface of the earth is mv!2/r.
[where "!" = upright arrow - BC]

Let us consider the acceleration
due to this, so we can compare
it with gravity's value of 32
feet per second squared. With
your figure, (near enough for
present purposes) the radius of
the earth is 4000*5280 feet.

The velocity at the equator is
such that a distance of 2*pi*r
is covered in 24 hours, or in
24*3600 seconds. This shows that
the centripetal acceleration is
(2*pi*4000*5280)!2/
(24*3600)!2*(4000*5280) feet per
second squared, and this comes
out at 0.11, i.e., a very small
fraction of g. I should add
that, as a mathematician, I was
always bad at 'sums', so I hope
others will check the above.

Your reason does not seem a good
one for moving eskimos to the
equator. However, because the
earth is not a perfect sphere,
but bulges out at the equator,
you are actually further away
from the centre of the earth
there, so gravity is less.
Specifically, one of my
reference books quotes 32.09
approx at the equator and 32.26
approx at the North Pole. Of
course, the earth's bulge is due
to its rotation.

Although this shows that the
centripetal acceleration is very
small, it is also true that
gravity is a very weak force.
(You may not believe it when you
drop a hammer on your big toe).

I came across a very graphic
illustration of this some years
ago. If you use a small perm-
anent magnet, perhaps an inch
long, to lift up a nail, then
the magnet is exerting a greater
upwards force on the nail than
the downwards pull of the earth.
When you consider that the
magnet weighs perhaps 20 grams
and the earth weighs about 6E27
grams, you can see the point!

I notice various comments where
readers are unhappy with the
service they are receiving from
firms. Whilst it is by no means
the answer in all cases, I
suggest that those concerned
should consider the possibility
of sueing the firms in the Small
Claims Court.

There are, of course, snags if
the firm has,or may, cease trad-
ing, but otherwise the threat of
a summons sometimes calls forth
a quick response. The procedures
are quite simple, and if other
courts are as helpful as is my
local one, then all the advice
you need is readily available.
It is not an expensive exercise.

Malcolm Perry comments that
SCART is not standard. It is a
matter of semantics to some
extent, but I believe that SCART
a standard - the villain in the
piece in this case is MGT/SAMCo,
who fitted an interface which
does not comply with the stand-
ard - which they are fully
entitled to do - and then

labelled it SCART, which in my
view they should not have done.
More, I have never seen why they
could not have implemented the
standard correctly.

On running Disk Scanner, a
comment appears on the screen:
"note that blank sectors are not
necessarily free for use". I
suspect that this is one of
yours - nobody else uses LET
O=0,I=1 ! Could you say what
this remark means, please?
You clearly are suffering with
the SAMCO Newsdisk. Had you had
the most recent issue, you would
have seen a discussion of the
new low-cost SAM, which is
broadly as you describe it.

                   Alan D. Cox.

Brian Cavers to Alan D. Cox

I wonder why SELF and IRIS are
used? I'd have thought "sender"
and "receiver" perfectly under-
standable! No, I'd never heard
those expressions before - at
least, I don't remember them but
then, I have not had much to do
with networking literature!

I would have thought data rates
could be varied. Even the humble
Interface 1 has variable baud
rates!

I am beginning to think I may
have to put back my Eskimos'
dieting plans until commercial
economy flights into orbit
become available.

However, studying both your and
Nanook's own reply (see Spectrum
OUTLETTERS) it seems there are
THREE factors to take into
account at the equator...

1. The greater MASS between
   eskimo and Earth's centre.

2. The greater DISTANCE between
   eskimo and Earth's centre due
   to the Earth's bulge (I seem
   to recall the term "oblate
   spheroid" from my schooldays)

3. The greater CENTRIFUGAL FORCE
   acting on the Eskimo (My
   dictionary says "centripetal"
   is a force PULLING to a
   centre (like gravity)whereas
   "centrifugal" is a force
   PUSHING AWAY FROM a centre.

If, as your and Nanook's letters
suggest, 1 and 2 cancel out then
3 is left so there may still be
a difference in the weight of an
eskimo at the Pole and Equator.

Furthermore, the figures you
quote: "32.09 approx. at the
equator and 32.26 approx at the
North Pole" I take to mean in
feet per second squared, that is
the speed of an object dropped
at the equator (forgetting about
air resistance for a minute)
would increase by 32.09 feet
per second each second. If this
is true then there really IS a
difference as I thought.It seems
about a hundred-and-ninetyeth
which means a 190lb eskimo would
weigh 1lb LESS at the equator!

That's quite a significant diff-
erence! I don't know whether it
would be enough to make a
success of my diet plans but I
reckon most eskimos would sweat
of a few more pounds at the
equator anyway - especially with
all those furs and blubber.

Can I put this eskimo down now
please?

I noticed some discs showed more
blank sectors in DISC SCANNER
than the DIR. I think it is when
a file has an end sector which
is full of zeros. I believe only
the first sector used by a file
has a header and subsequent ones
only use the last two bytes to
point to the next sector and its
track.

The last two bytes of the final
sector are, I think, two zeros.
Therefore, if you reset your SAM
so RAM is full of zeros and SAVE
"TEST" CODE 50000,1000 then I
think the final sector will be
all zeros. It would show as a
"blank" sector in the Disc
Scanner program yet would not be
free for use with normal saves
because the directory bitmap
would have it flagged as part of
the "TEST" file.

Two nil to me I think.

                         -Brian

From: Ken Bower, HUNTINGDON

Dear Ron and Brian,

I would like to point out that
every issue since and including
the Xmas Issue that I have
received has either crashed on
BOOTing or crashed during some
of the programs.

I have found by omitting the
procedure SAMCHARS that the disk
BOOTs up O.K. and I therefore
think that the code has become
corrupted for some reason and
would appreciate your advice on
this matter.

Many thanks for OUTLET which I
look forward to receiving every
month.               - Ken Bower

Brian Cavers to Ken Bower

With SAMCHARS, TEXAT and other
OUTLET routines I have always
been very wary of running these
machine code programs at around
16384 because I suspected system
or other SAMCo routines may use
that area temporarily. I have,
therefore,taken care to use that
area only temporarily myself.
That is, TEXAT and SAMCHARS only
place the code there as needed,
CALL it and then abandon it. If
any other alien code should
corrupt the area later it
doesn't matter as my routines
replace their code into position
there EACH TIME they are needed.

HOWEVER!!...

I have recently discovered that
several SAMCO routines, DUMP,
SOUND MACHINE MUSIC and others,
not only temporarily use that
area but PERMANENTLY place a
vector around there! This means
they reserve the place for
themselves and any other code
that uses that area will crash!

This seems to me to be a misuse
of memory. I know of no info
being issued about this and
routines like DUMP and music,
that are intended for use in
other programs (i.e. not stand-
alone programs like a word-
processor) ought to be more
compatible or,at the very least,
information about their memory
use ought to be included with
the software.

Anyway, there is nothing wrong
with SAMCHARS but I have changed
it from this issue onward to use
a higher address (you just alter
the POKE).

Meanwhile, you should RESET your
machine before booting OUTLET as
you are almost certainly loading
something else before OUTLET
(What?!). If it still does not
work then either you have a
different version machine to
everyone else (enter PRINT PEEK
15 and tell me what you get) or
your machine is faulty.

In the long term I shall have to
think of a different method of
CALLing code but it is a flaming
nuisance!(not your fault!)-Brian

Brian Cavers to all


Here are a couple of tips...

On both Spectrum Disciple/+D and
SAM Coupe, if you want to check
how much room there is left on a
disc then you list a directory
with CAT or DIR. However, in 9
cases out of 10, the very fact
that you are checking is because
you know already that particular
disc is fairly full - right? It
follows that the directory list
will be tediously long and slow
before you see the free space at
the end.

A quick way of displaying the K
FREE only is as follows...

Enter...

CAT 1""""     (DISCIPLE)

DIR 1""""     (SAM)

That is, the normal command plus
four quotation marks. This gives
a directory restricted to names
beginning with a quotation mark.
I don't know about you, but in
my case that is always zero! I
never put a quotation mark in a
filename. Therefore, all you get
is the kilobytes free and it is
much faster.

You could, of course, use any
single rare character within two
quotation marks like "@" but the
quotation marks are on one key!

My second tip is SAM only - for
use with the SOUND MACHINE.

The built-in looping system does
seem to be limited to the whole
piece of music yet music often
has an intro followed by several
choruses etc. and it sounds a
bit odd if you loop back to the
intro for music that you want to
repeat as background.You can set
up a loop on some channels only
but if you need all the channels
you can't reserve any!

My method is to POKE the address
of the code +1620 with a value
AFTER the music has started
playing. The address is the one
referred to as PAGEADDR in the
bit of BASIC, as follows...

      DPOKE PAGEADDR+1620,n

     ...where n is (I think) the
number of notes from the start
divided by 2. I said "I think"
because I just found it by
experimenting (with the title
music to this issue) until it
was right. The answer in that
case was to DPOKE 64 and there
looked to be about 32 notes in
the intro - at a guess!

You must put the POKE after the
music has started playing or it
will be ignored because the code
itself POKEs that address in its
initialization sequence.

If anyone knows a better way,let
us know!
                        - Brian

From: John A. Boylan, Co. Down

Dear OUTLET Editors,

I would like to thank you for the opportunity to obtain your great Disk-Mag at such a fantastic price as I had the misfortune to suffer the misplacement of most of my disks and mail last year and unfortun- ately had my OUTLET disks wiped and paper communication lost.

Having no record of your address, and being a Retained Firefighter with very little time, I never got around to recontacting you until your offer came in the post.

I use my SAM 512 TWIN DRIVE to keep the minutes of our local Divisional Fire Brigade Aid Fund and to keep up with any of our members, serving or retired, to ensure that we can offer assist- ance when required by them.

I use Tasword 2 for most of my work in this but as I am finding a little difficulty in keeping accounts and records only using TW2, could you recommend a cheap or free Spreadsheet/Database that would assist me?

The easiest method of sorting strings is known as the BUBBLE SORT. It is not the fastest way but it is the simplest to follow how it works. Try this...

10 LET SWAP=0

20 FOR N=1 TO 7 (Your 8 minus 1)

30 IF VAL T$(N)<VAL T$(N+1) THEN LET Q$=T$(N): LET T$(N)=T$(N+1):     (swap) LET T$(N+1)=Q$: LET SWAP=1

40 NEXT N

50 IF SWAP=1 THEN GOTO 10

To reverse the order, change the "<" in line 30 to a ">". If you are only using values up to 9 then you can omit the two "VAL" statements in line 30 and it will go faster. It will also go faster if you use a numeric array to store the values. Very large arrays will be VERY slow to sort in BASIC!

Brian Cavers to all

Here are a couple of tips...

On both Spectrum Disciple/+D and SAM Coupe, if you want to check how much room there is left on a disc then you list a directory with CAT or DIR. However, in 9 cases out of 10, the very fact that you are checking is because you know already that particular disc is fairly full - right? It follows that the directory list will be tediously long and slow before you see the free space at the end.

A quick way of displaying the K FREE only is as follows...

Enter...

CAT 1""""     (DISCIPLE)

DIR 1""""     (SAM)

That is, the normal command plus four quotation marks. This gives a directory restricted to names beginning with a quotation mark. I don't know about you, but in my case that is always zero! I never put a quotation mark in a filename. Therefore, all you get is the kilobytes free and it is much faster.

You could, of course, use any single rare character within two quotation marks like "@" but the quotation marks are on one key!

My second tip is SAM only - for use with the SOUND MACHINE.

The built-in looping system does seem to be limited to the whole piece of music yet music often has an intro followed by several choruses etc. and it sounds a bit odd if you loop back to the intro for music that you want to repeat as background.You can set up a loop on some channels only but if you need all the channels you can't reserve any!

My method is to POKE the address of the code +1620 with a value AFTER the music has started playing. The address is the one referred to as PAGEADDR in the bit of BASIC, as follows...

DPOKE PAGEADDR+1620,n

...where n is (I think) the number of notes from the start divided by 2. I said "I think" because I just found it by experimenting (with the title music to this issue) until it was right. The answer in that case was to DPOKE 64 and there looked to be about 32 notes in the intro - at a guess!

You must put the POKE after the music has started playing or it will be ignored because the code itself POKEs that address in its initialization sequence.

If anyone knows a better way,let us know!

То есть TEXAT и SAMCHARS просто помещают туда код по мере необходимости, вызывают его через CALL и тут же забывают. Если какой-либо чужой код позже испортит эту область, не страшно — мои подпрограммы заново копируют свой код на место КАЖДЫЙ РАЗ, когда он требуется.

ОДНАКО!!...

Недавно я выяснил, что некоторые фирменные процедуры SAMCO — DUMP, SOUND MACHINE MUSIC и другие — не просто временно используют эту область, они НАВСЕГДА вешают туда вектор! Это означает, что они резервируют это место под себя, и любой другой код, использующий эту область, неизбежно вызовет сбой!

На мой взгляд, это совершенно неграмотное распоряжение памятью. Мне не попадалось никакой документации на этот счет, а ведь подпрограммы вроде DUMP и музыки, рассчитанные на внедрение в другие программы (в отличие от самостоятельных приложений вроде текстовых процессоров), должны быть более совместимыми — или, по крайней мере, сведения об используемой ими памяти должны прилагаться к софту.

В общем, в самой SAMCHARS ошибок нет, но начиная с этого номера я перенес ее на более высокий адрес (достаточно просто изменить POKE).

А пока что вам следует нажимать RESET перед загрузкой OUTLET, поскольку вы почти наверняка запускаете что-то еще до OUTLET (Что именно?!). Если это все равно не поможет, то либо у вас другая ревизия машины, не как у всех (введите PRINT PEEK 15 и напишите мне, что получилось), либо ваш компьютер неисправен.

В долгосрочной перспективе мне придется придумать другой метод вызова машинного кода через CALL, но это жуткая морока! (не по вашей вине!)

Вот пара полезных советов...

И на Spectrum Disciple/+D, и на SAM Coupe, когда вам нужно узнать, сколько места осталось на диске, вы выводите каталог с помощью CAT или DIR. Однако в 9 случаях из 10 вы проверяете это именно потому, что уже знаете: данный диск забит почти под завязку — верно? Соответственно, вывод каталога будет утомительно долгим и медленным, прежде чем в самом конце вы увидите заветные свободные килобайты.

Вот быстрый способ вывести ТОЛЬКО остаток K FREE...

Введите...

```text
CAT 1""""     (DISCIPLE)

DIR 1""""     (SAM)
```

То есть обычная команда плюс четыре кавычки. Это выведет каталог, ограниченный только теми именами, которые начинаются с кавычки. Не знаю, как у вас, но в моём случае таких файлов всегда ноль! Я никогда не ставлю кавычку в имя файла. Соответственно, всё, что вы получаете — это количество свободных килобайтов, и работает это намного быстрее.

Конечно, можно было бы использовать любой редкий символ внутри двух кавычек, например, `"@"`, но ведь кавычки находятся на одной клавише!

Мой второй совет касается только SAM — для работы с SOUND MACHINE.

Встроенная система зацикливания, похоже, ограничена только всей композицией целиком, тогда как в музыке часто есть вступление, за которым следует несколько припевов и т.д., и звучит довольно странно, когда трек, который вы хотите крутить фоном, снова и снова возвращается во вступление. Можно настроить петлю только для некоторых каналов, но если вам нужны все каналы, выделить отдельный не получится!

Мой метод заключается в том, чтобы сделать POKE по адресу кода +1620 определённым значением ПОСЛЕ того, как музыка начала играть. Этот адрес упоминается как PAGEADDR в кусочке на BASIC, вот так:

```text
      DPOKE PAGEADDR+1620,n
```

...где n — это (как мне кажется) количество нот от начала, разделённое на 2. Я говорю «как мне кажется», потому что подобрал это экспериментально (на заглавной музыке к этому номеру), пока не заработало как надо. В том случае решением было сделать DPOKE 64, а во вступлении, на глаз, было около 32 нот!

Вы обязательно должны делать POKE уже после запуска музыки, иначе команда проигнорируется, так как сам код прописывает POKE по этому адресу во время своей инициализации.

Если кто-то знает способ получше — дайте нам знать!  
— Brian
